raw_response:
I have farmed a long time, so I will not play fancy with it. On 10.9 mu, with only two people in the house, I will keep the whole field in cotton and do it the way that is steady. If the seed other people around me planted did well, I will use that improved seed, not old leftover seed. Before sowing I will plough the land once, put the base fertilizer in, and get the soil loose enough so the seedlings come up even. Cotton eats fertilizer in the middle and later stages, but I do not want the early plants to grow too wild, so I will not dump everything at one time. I will aim around 13 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu for the whole season, then split it between base fertilizer and later topdressing. Since I have well irrigation, I will plan on 4 waterings if the year is normal: one after stand establishment if the ground is dry, one at budding, one at flowering and boll setting, and one later if the plants still hold fruit well. Cotton insects here can turn bad quickly, and losing bolls hurts more than spending a little more on spray, so I will expect about 5 pesticide rounds through the season, watching aphids, mites, bollworm, and mirids. If the weather goes well, I will count on about 320 kg seed cotton per mu. That is a number I can work toward without dreaming too high.
